content: 1. When co-administering levomilnacipran, do not exceed a daily dose of 80 mg. This is due to potential interactions with other drugs that may increase its plasma levels or effects. 2. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine) by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug in such cases. 3. Cobicistat can also increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate (oral) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised, and caution should be exercised. 4. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma hormone concentrations, necessitating the use of alternative drugs or close monitoring. 5. Darunavir can increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate (oral) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 6. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels (increase or decrease) may occur with certain drug interactions, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 7. Darunavir increases lidocaine levels by reducing its metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and caution should be exercised. 8. Cobicistat also increases lidocaine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administering antiarrhythmics. 9. Darunavir decreases the effects of linagliptin through mechanisms that may involve CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. Darunavir increases linagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjustments to therapy and close monitoring are necessary. 11. Darunavir decreases liraglutide effects, potentially due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Hyperglycemia should be monitored closely. 12. Darunavir increases lofexidine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia should be monitored, and dose reduction of lofexidine may be necessary. 13. Darunavir increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 14. Cobicistat also increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Darunavir increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 16. Cobicistat increases lonafarnib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be co-administered with lonafarnib due to significant interactions. 18. Darunavir increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 19. Lopinavir increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but also decreases darunavir levels by enhancing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Darunavir increases loratadine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Lorlatinib decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Darunavir increases lorlatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 23. If co-administration of lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the inhibitor is discontinued, return to the previous lorlatinib dose after 3 plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 24. Darunavir increases losartan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 25. Cobicistat increases losartan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 26. Cobicistat increases lovastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 27. Darunavir also increases lovastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase systemic statin exposure, raising the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 29. Darunavir increases levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 30. Cobicistat increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 31. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to 1 tablet daily for the first week to allow for steady-state induction effects. Afterward, continue with the recommended daily dose. 32. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors when co-administered with lumacaftor/ivacaftor. 33. Darunavir increases lumateperone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Cobicistat also increases lumateperone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 35. Darunavir increases lurasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Cobicistat increases lurasidone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 37. Darunavir increases lurbinectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50% if unavoidable. 38. Cobicistat also increases lurbinectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50% if unavoidable. 39. Darunavir increases macitentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Cobicistat increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. Darunavir also increases maraviroc levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 42. Marijuana increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 43. Darunavir increases marijuana levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 44. Darunavir increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure from systolic dysfunction. 45. Cobicistat also increases mavacamten levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 46. Darunavir increases mavorixafor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 47. Cobicistat increases mavorixafor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 48. Darunavir increases medroxyprogesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 49. Darunavir decreases medroxyprogesterone levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Cobicistat increases mefloquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to the potential for increased toxicity. 51. Darunavir also increases mefloquine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration due to the potential for increased toxicity. 52. Darunavir increases meperidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 53. Darunavir increases mestranol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 54. Darunavir decreases metformin effects, potentially due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Hyperglycemia should be monitored closely. 55. Cobicistat increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 56. Darunavir also increases methadone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 57. Cobicistat increases methylergonovine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of acute ergot toxicity. 58. Darunavir also increases methylergonovine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 59. Methylprednisolone decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 60. Cobicistat increases methylprednisolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 61. Darunavir increases methylprednisolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 62. Darunavir increases metoclopramide intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid co-administration as dose adjustment is not feasible. 63. Darunavir increases metoprolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 64. Cobicistat also increases metoprolol levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 65. Metronidazole increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required.
